name: InlineMessage
statusNote: InlineMessage is alpha and is exported from @primer/react/experimental, so its import path may still change. It passed an accessibility review on 2025-01-08.
summary: A short status line, an icon and coloured text, placed next to the thing it describes (a form field, a row, a section). Choose it over Banner when the message is part of the flow rather than a standalone landmark; it has no background, border, title or actions.

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: The message (children): text, optionally with inline links. It fills the second grid column.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Intent: picks the text and icon colour and the default icon. The docs mark it required; the code accepts none and then draws a neutral InfoIcon message in the default foreground.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Body-small (12px) or body-medium (14px) text; small also swaps to 12px filled icons.

inputs.name: leadingVisual
inputs.description: A custom icon (or any node) in place of the variant's icon. A component type is rendered with the icon class but no size, so an octicon comes out at its 16px default even at size small.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: A two-column grid (auto | 1fr) with an 8px column gap, top-aligned, setting font size, line height and colour for both columns.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: The variant's octicon in the text colour (octicons fill with currentColor), given a minimum height of one line box so it centres on the first line.

anatomy.name: Message
anatomy.description: The children, in the second column, wrapping freely.

variants.description: No variant: InfoIcon (16px at both sizes) in the default foreground.
Danger text; AlertIcon at medium, AlertFillIcon at small.
Attention text; AlertIcon at medium, AlertFillIcon at small.
Success text; CheckCircleIcon at medium, CheckCircleFillIcon at small.
Muted text for something that cannot be used; AlertIcon at medium, AlertFillIcon at small.
14px text at the medium body line height (21px); 16px outline icons.
12px text at the small body line height (19.5px); 12px filled icons.

layout.text: Lay the message out as a two-column grid: the icon column sizes to the icon, the message column takes the rest; the columns are 8px apart and both align to the top.
The icon's minimum height is the line height times the font size (19.5px small, 21px medium), so a 12px or 16px glyph sits centred on the first line of text however many lines the message wraps to.
Icons are 16px at medium (and for no variant or a component-type leadingVisual at either size) and 12px at small for the four variants.

states.text: The whole message, text and icon, takes the variant's foreground colour: --fgColor-danger, --fgColor-attention, --fgColor-success or --fgColor-muted, else --fgColor-default.

behaviour.text: InlineMessage is static: it has no interaction, no dismissal and no motion. Showing or hiding it is the caller's job.

keyboard: Not focusable; links inside the message keep their own keyboard behaviour.
semantics: No role and no live region: a message that appears after user input is not announced unless the caller puts it in a live region or ties it to its control (aria-describedby).
Colour is never the only signal: each variant pairs its colour with a distinct icon, and the text must say what happened.
The icon carries no text alternative; the message text must stand alone.

notes.text: The container is a CSS grid, so every child node becomes its own grid item: text followed by a link would spill onto a second row under the icon. Pass the message as one element. A native build should treat the children as one text flow in the second column.
Without a variant the icon is InfoIcon at 16px even at size small, and the colour is --fgColor-default; only the four variants get 12px filled icons at small.
The 8px (0.5rem) column gap is a literal. The line-height fallbacks 1.6666 and 1.4285 are stale: the tokens resolve to 1.625 and 1.5, so the fallbacks never apply and do not match.
The docs mark variant required and spell one value 'unvailable'; the code makes variant optional and spells it 'unavailable'.

Announcement is left to the browser's live-region machinery, which InlineMessage does not even opt into. A native build that wants dynamic messages announced must post them to the platform accessibility API itself.
